summary.oneLiner: Legacy RPSF/fibre business has decisively turned the corner this quarter (best volume in 5 years, margin recovery on stable scrap), while the high-optionality food-grade rPET subsidiary remains stranded at ~50% utilisation pending the long-delayed PWMR relaxation notification — management firmly defers the rPET inflection to FY27, when the 40% recycled-content mandate is "intact" and offtake should be forced.

thesis (one-liner): Legacy RPSF/fibre business has decisively turned the corner this quarter (best volume in 5 years, margin recovery on stable scrap), while the high-optionality food-grade rPET subsidiary remains stranded at ~50% utilisation pending the long-delayed PWMR relaxation notification — management firmly defers the rPET inflection to FY27, when the 40% recycled-content mandate is "intact" and offtake should be forced.
scorecard (q3fy26):
**Standalone (legacy RPSF/fibre/yarn):**
| Metric | Q3FY26 | Q2FY26 | QoQ | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | ₹272.95 cr | ₹259.35 cr | +5.24% | Best volume in 5 yrs |
| EBITDA | ₹18.54 cr | — | — | Margin 6.79% vs 3.15% in Q2 |
| EBITDA/ton | ₹5,962 | ₹2,812 | +112% | Still well below FY24/25 norm (~₹9–10k target) |
| Sales volume | 31,107 MT | — | +7% | Highest in 5 years; >1 lakh MT expected full-year |
| Production volume | 29,088 MT | 25,689 MT | +13% | Capacity util >100% |

**Consolidated (incl. rPET subsidiary):**
| Metric | Q3FY26 | Q2FY26 | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | ₹357.22 cr | ~marginally higher | Standalone ₹272.95cr + subsidiary ₹84.27cr |
| EBITDA | ₹30.73 cr | ₹22.3 cr (implied) | +37.67% QoQ; standalone ₹18.54cr + sub ₹12.19cr |
| EBITDA margin | 8.6% | — | Subsidiary EBITDA margin 14.5% |
| EBITDA/ton | ₹7,638 | ₹5,703 | — |
| PAT (reported) | ₹4.74 cr (consol) | — | Standalone PAT ₹15.94 cr (surpassed prior 2 qtrs combined) |
| Production (consol) | 38,768 MT | — | — |

**CALL-OUT — PET-bottle scrap cost & rPET ramp:** Scrap bottle price ₹46–47/kg, "pretty stable" this quarter vs high volatility in prior 2 quarters — the single biggest driver of legacy margin recovery. rPET subsidiary (Warangal) ramp STALLED: capacity utilisation dropped to ~50%, revenue down ~23% QoQ, because the draft PWMR relaxation notification's extraordinary delay froze brand-owner offtake of rPET granules (~90% of brands have not started buying in proper volume; holding purchases since December awaiting final notification). Realizations: Fibre ~₹85/kg, Granules >₹95/kg. No normalised PAT bridge given (one-off: received ₹70 cr in Jan from Telangana Govt out of ~₹110 cr Warangal incentive outstanding — balance-sheet/cash item, not P&L).
guidance (critical — explicit):
- **Legacy volume:** >1,00,000 MT for full FY26 (already 31,107 MT in Q3).
- **Legacy margin:** Back to **9%–10% EBITDA margin** / **₹9,000–10,000 EBITDA/ton** (FY24/25 levels) in FY27; Q4FY26 better than Q3. Earlier guidance was 10% for Q4FY26 / ~11% FY27 — now framed as "come back to 9–10% next year"; declined to upgrade.
- **rPET / subsidiary utilisation:** Q4FY26 capacity util **70%–80%** (vs 50% in Q3, includes brownfield); FY27 util **85%–90%**.
- **rPET volume FY27:** ~70,000 MT capacity → expecting **55,000–60,000+ MT** volume.
- **rPET peak revenue potential:** **₹700–850 cr** at ~70,000 MT (Warangal) once util picks up.
- **rPET margin FY27:** Declined to give a number ("market evolving, will comment next quarter"); reiterated "will do much better."
- **rPET mix:** **65% of revenue from rPET by FY28** guidance reaffirmed as intact.
- **Capex:** Brownfield ~₹130 cr (≈22,500 MT rPET, Warangal) — largely incurred, operational Mar/Apr-2026. Next leg (brownfield/greenfield) **~₹450 cr over next 2 years**; funded internally, leverage "very comfortable," no fresh raise needed.
- **Overall:** Q4FY26 better than both Q2 and Q3, aided by BOTH legacy and subsidiary.
demand:
- Legacy: Strong — best volume in 5 yrs; US tariff cut on Indian textiles to give additional boost; >35% of volume now from non-woven & home furnishing (de-risking from yarn spinning).
- rPET granules (B2B/F&B): Weak — brand-owner offtake stalled awaiting notification; F&B demand "improved" QoQ but "still not to the level expected." Brands currently at only ~10–15% recycled content (global majors); not ramping until MoEF clarity. Real demand inflection expected Q1FY27 onward.
segment colour:
- **RPSF/legacy fibre:** Recovered; >100% util; margin rebound on stable scrap. Filament yarn qualified with a **leading global textile brand** — offtake starts Feb-2026, expected to add 20–30% to filament capacity utilisation, "quite good" margins (not disclosed).
- **rPET/granules (Ganesha Ecopet, Warangal):** 50% util, rev −23% QoQ; the swing factor for FY27.
- **Value-added:** Non-woven + home furnishing >35% of volume — reduces yarn-spinning dependency. Became regular supplier to ICC (stadium flags from recycled material) — branding/sustainability proof point.
growth / optionality:
- **Food-grade rPET** is the core multi-year optionality — 65% rev mix by FY28 reaffirmed; FY27 the forced-adoption year as 40% mandate is "live and intact."
- **EPR-driven demand:** PWMR mandate ramps 30%→40%→...→60% (FY26→FY29). Penalties escalate (₹2,900 → ₹5,800 → ₹8,700/ton for successive defaults) + Environmental Compensation; non-compliance not absolved by penalty (carries forward). Strong structural pull.
- **Approved industry capacity** now ~2,50,000–3,00,000 MT — enough for FY27 mandate; Ganesha positioned as "largest capacity holder."
- **Exports:** ~9–10% of fibre volume; >₹100 cr in 9M, ~₹30 cr in Q3 (consol). US route blocked since 2-Sep (rPET removed from tariff exemption, 50% reciprocal tariff). If US tariff drops to 18%, exploring re-entry — uncertain on viability.
- **Polyolefins recycling:** Early-stage exploration beyond PET (plan not finalised).
margins & cost:
- Legacy margin fully driven by PET-bottle **scrap availability/cost** — ₹46–47/kg stable vs prior volatility; mgmt maintains ~30–35 days inventory (40 in summer); scrap is unorganised, cannot over-stock.
- Subsidiary margin (14.5% this qtr) hit by low util + oversupply (13 FSSAI-approved players now vs 5–6 earlier) → price pressure; expected to "relax to some level" next year as demand catches supply.
- Realizations flat — supply >> demand; no improvement until offtake firms post-notification.
capex (rpet expansion ramp):
- Brownfield ~₹130 cr (≈22,500 MT rPET, Warangal) — largely spent, live Mar/Apr-2026 (included in Q4 70% util).
- Next leg ~₹450 cr over 2 years (brownfield + greenfield).
- FY27 Warangal rPET capacity ~70,000 MT.
capital allocation:
- Capex self-funded; leverage "very comfortable," no fresh equity/debt raise flagged.
- Received ₹70 cr in Jan-2026 from Telangana Govt (of ~₹110 cr Warangal incentive outstanding) — improves cash.
risks:
- **Scrap cost/availability:** unorganised collection; fibre vs B2B competition for PET bottles is pushing fibre industry toward textile/other waste (relieves some pressure). Winter reduces N-India scrap availability.
- **Virgin-polyester / oversupply competition:** 13 FSSAI players, capacity >> demand → realization & margin pressure in rPET.
- **Regulatory/ramp execution:** Entire FY26 rPET thesis hostage to PWMR notification timing; if FY27 adoption again slips, key risk. Mgmt firm it won't (40% mandate intact, no further relaxation expected for FY27).
- **Tariff:** US 50% reciprocal tariff blocks rPET exports; 18% (if cut) may still be too high.
- **New entrants:** Reliance–Sri Chakra (RPSF, legacy product), Indorama–Varun Beverages JV (rPET) — JV volumes already factored; mgmt downplays (industry highly competitive for 25 yrs, Ganesha remains leader).
management tone: Confident and concrete on legacy turnaround; candid and measured on rPET delay ("extraordinary delay has defeated the purpose"); repeatedly deferred firm rPET margin guidance to next quarter (genuine uncertainty, not evasion). Conviction that FY27 is the delayed-by-one-year inflection. Notably transparent on penalty mechanics and competitive landscape.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The ₹70 cr Telangana incentive receipt (Jan) is a cash event easily missed in P&L analysis.
- Filament-yarn qualification with a global textile brand (offtake Feb, +20–30% filament util) is an under-discussed near-term margin/volume kicker, separate from the rPET story.
- Mechanical-recycling moat: mgmt explicitly rules out chemical recycling (capex/opex too high, not commercially viable) — counters the "Reliance chemical-recycling threat" narrative.
- Paying the EPR penalty does NOT absolve the recycled-content obligation (carries forward) — structurally forces eventual offtake; brand-equity cost of penalties is high for majors.
- FY26 rPET realizations move with scrap-bottle price (pass-through), so margin is util-driven, not price-driven.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ⭐ Ganesha itself = primary FY27 beneficiary of forced PWMR compliance (40% mandate, largest capacity).
- ✅ rPET/recycled-content theme broadly: peers also benefit from EPR mandate ramp.
- (No external named beneficiaries beyond the sector theme.)

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.

themes.title: Specialty packaging & sustainable materials
themes.need: Premiumization, e-commerce and a sustainability/recycling mandate drive a packaging up-cycle across flexible films, rigid plastics, cartons and compostables. UFLEX/EPL/HUHTAMAKI/COSMOFIRST/ESTER on films/tubes; TCPLPACK/AGI/BOROLTD on cartons/glass; MOLDTKPAC/MOLDTECH on rigid/IML; PAKKA/GANECOS on compostable & recycled materials.
themes.driver: Brand-owner restocking; export demand recovery; recycled-content mandates; commodity-cost pass-through.
